Figure 1:Overview.Given (a) an image pair and sparse correspondences (colored dot clicks),Click3Rconditions DUSt3R[44]to produce accurate 3D reconstruction. (b) DUSt3R fails on a scene with limited overlaps.
(c) With as few as two clicks,Click3Rrecovers correct geometry.

Figure 2:Click3Rarchitecture.A shared ViT encoder processes the two input images. Correspondence prompts are tokenized using our correspondence tokenizer (Section3.2). A symmetric point correspondence adapter, implemented as a lightweight transformer with self-attention and cross-attention (Section3.3), updates the decoder-input features for each view. The asymmetric decoder then interprets the updated embeddings and passes them to the original DUSt3R[44]heads to predict 3D pointmaps and confidence.

Figure 3:Hard3DBench.Statistics shown for the 2-view stereo subset of Hard3DBench.
(a) Hard3DBench produces substantially larger pretrained DUSt3R rotation errors than the regular benchmark.
(b) Failure category distribution.
(c) Example image pairs in Hard3DBench.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparison.Each example features challenging geometry, such as large baselines, limited co-visibility, or substantial viewpoint changes. The input image pair with user-provided correspondence prompts (colored dots) is shown on the left, followed by each model’s reconstruction.Click3Rproduces more accurate and consistent 3D reconstructions, with prompted correspondences aligning more closely in 3D. Additional qualitative results are provided in AppendixFigure13.

Without prompts (middle), attention is diffuse.
